lens: human connection, trust, agency, communication, collaboration

findings.observation: The loaded package says it collects only visible pixels or an explicit selection, keeps exact evidence reviewable, supports Remove and minimization, stays silent on capture API handoff before explicit Submit, and labels all exercised content synthetic; the harness still cannot show the user's Google Chrome toolbar gesture and positive temporary activeTab grant.
findings.user_impact: The review surface treats candidate conversation evidence with restraint, but a live recruiter cannot yet rely on this run to prove that real evidence enters only through the promised visible gesture.
findings.recommendation: Record one policy-authorized Google Chrome toolbar or shortcut capture of synthetic conversation content, keeping the exact selected asset visible until explicit Submit.
findings.verification: The recording shows the gesture, temporary source scope, exact review, optional minimization or removal, no capture handoff before Submit, and no action beyond one localhost capture receipt.

findings.observation: The UI explains three requested retention modes and explicitly says a receipt does not prove deletion; after the synthetic text receipt it distinguishes Deleted locally from unverified backend derivative deletion. No candidate-facing notice, recruiter agreement, or backend retention/deletion behavior is part of the frozen artifact.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-2/browser-extension/18-local-deleted-backend-unverified-390.png; docs/evaluations/round-2/browser-extension/review-object.json boundary and environment; apps/browser-extension/README.md Honest development limits
findings.user_impact: The interface avoids a deceptive deletion promise, while a live deployment would still need a humane, comprehensible explanation of why conversation evidence is captured and how long every derivative persists.
findings.recommendation: Before real candidate data, pair the extension with reviewed notice, purpose, retention, deletion, and recruiter-responsibility language tied to implemented backend controls.
findings.verification: A recruiter can accurately explain the purpose and lifecycle before importing real evidence, and source plus registered derivatives follow the selected policy in backend readback.

strengths: The blocked fixture says candidate scoring or ranking is outside the product boundary; no candidate worth, fit, personality, tone, protected trait, or acceptance probability is displayed.
The no-action fixture states that insufficient evidence creates no task, avoiding manufactured urgency or pressure on the candidate.
Every proposed fact and the single bounded question remain tied to exact observed words, while the UI repeatedly says the fixture is proposed and never confirmed candidate state.
The extension makes no contact, calendar, ATS, message, or other external write and describes the Submit effect as one capture handoff only.
Permission denial, offline, unknown, stale session, retry, receipt, Remove, and local deletion use candid language about what happened and what remains safe.
missing_evidence: User-visible Google Chrome gesture and positive temporary source grant.
Candidate-facing notice or consent-policy evaluation for real private conversation evidence.
Implemented backend retention and derivative deletion.
open_questions: What notice and accountability language will accompany the first use of real candidate conversation evidence?
